gapFill.title: Fill in the gaps
gapFill.subtitle: 20 original sentences covering an action before another past action, reasons and results, experience before a point (already / just / never), negatives, and questions — always with had, never have/has.

questions.explain: Leaving happened before you arrived — the earlier of two past actions.

questions.before: By the time he called, I
questions.explain: 'Go' is irregular: the past participle is gone, not went.

questions.before: By the time her friends knocked on the door, she
questions.explain: She finished before her friends knocked — 'by the time' needs had + past participle (regular: finished).

questions.before: By the time he left the house, he
questions.explain: 'Eat' is irregular: the past participle is eaten, not ate. 'By the time' marks the later past moment.

questions.before: By the time we got to the stadium, the race
questions.explain: The race started before we got to the stadium — 'by the time' needs had + past participle.

questions.before: He fell asleep as soon as he got home — by then he
questions.explain: 'By then' points to a past moment; the walking was complete before it, which explains why he was so tired.

questions.before: The carpet was wet because the cat
questions.explain: The cat knocked the vase over shortly before — had just + past participle gives the earlier cause of the wet carpet.

questions.before: She felt confident on exam day: by then she
questions.after: every unit of the book twice.
questions.explain: 'By then' needs had + past participle. Consonant + y → change y to i before -ed: studied.

questions.before: When we got to the cinema, the film
questions.explain: 'Already' sits between had and the past participle.

questions.before: When we moved to Canada, I was amazed: I
questions.explain: 'See' is irregular: the past participle is seen, not saw. 'Never … before' looks back from a past moment.

questions.before: When I rang her at 9 p.m., she
questions.explain: 'Just' describes something completed a short time before the past moment of my call.

questions.after: the answer before he explained it.
questions.explain: She guessed before his explanation — 'already' goes between had and guessed.

questions.before: At our first restaurant in Japan, we were nervous because we
questions.explain: Consonant + y → change y to i before -ed: tried. 'Never … before' looks back from a past moment.
'Since Christmas' needs a perfect tense, and the story is past, so use hadn't + past participle: heard.

questions.before: By the time the meeting ended at three, I
questions.explain: 'Hadn't' + past participle — the participle of eat is eaten. 'By the time' marks the later past moment.

questions.after: the project, so they asked for more time.
questions.explain: 'By last Friday's deadline' is a past point: hadn't + past participle — never 'hadn't finish'.

questions.before: By her eightieth birthday, my grandma still
questions.after: a smartphone, so we gave her one as a present.
questions.explain: Negative past perfect: hadn't + past participle. Up to that birthday, she had no experience of smartphones.

questions.after: you heard of the band before that festival?
questions.explain: Past perfect questions start with 'had', whatever the subject.
'Had' + subject + past participle — the main verb stays in its participle form.

questions.after: he finished his work before the meeting started?
questions.explain: A question about which of two past events happened first.

wordOrder.title: Put it in order
wordOrder.subtitle: Tap the words to build each sentence — 20 examples covering an action before another past action, reasons and results, already/just/never, negatives, and questions.

matching.title: Match the past participles
matching.subtitle: Tap a base verb, then tap the past participle you'd use after "had". These twenty are the irregular ones learners confuse with the past simple form (had went instead of had gone).

timedMC.title: Beat the clock
timedMC.subtitle: 15 seconds per question. Watch for present-perfect traps (has/have instead of had) and irregular past participles (had gone, not had went).

questions.text: By the time we arrived, the shop       .
wrongReasons: Missing "had": without it, this just states a single past event, not the earlier of two.
Wrong tense: present perfect doesn't show which past action came first — use had.
Wrong tense: this needs had + past participle, not a background scene.
questions.explain: The closing happened before we arrived — the earlier of two past actions.

questions.text: When she opened the fridge, she realised someone        all the milk.
wrongReasons: Wrong participle: the past participle of drink is drunk, not drank.
Wrong auxiliary: an earlier past action needs had, not has.
After had, use the past participle (drunk), not the base form.
questions.explain: 'Drink' is irregular: the past participle is drunk, not drank.

questions.text: I couldn't get in because I        my keys at home.
wrongReasons: Wrong auxiliary: had, not have, for an action before another past action.
After had, use the past participle (left), not the base form.
"Leave" is irregular: leave → left → left. "Leaved" doesn't exist.
questions.explain: Leaving the keys is the earlier of two past events.

questions.text: By the time the ambulance arrived, the patient       .
wrongReasons: Wrong auxiliary: had, not has, for the earlier action.
Missing "had" before the past participle.
Wrong tense/structure for an action completed before a past point.
questions.explain: 'Already' confirms this finished before the ambulance's arrival.

questions.text: He was exhausted because he        all day.
wrongReasons: Wrong auxiliary: had, not has, for the earlier reason.
After had, use the past participle (travelled), not the base form.
The -ing form alone isn't a full verb — you need had + past participle.
questions.explain: Past perfect explains the reason: travelling happened before he felt exhausted.

questions.text: The grass was wet because it        during the night.
wrongReasons: Wrong auxiliary: had, not has — the story is in the past.
After had, use the past participle (rained), not the base form.
Wrong tense: present continuous doesn't fit a past story about last night.
questions.explain: The rain is the earlier cause of the later, wet-grass result.

questions.text: She felt proud because she        the marathon.
wrongReasons: Wrong auxiliary: had, not has, for the earlier reason.
After had, use the past participle (finished), not the base form.
The -ing form alone isn't a full verb — you need had + past participle.
questions.explain: Finishing the marathon is the earlier action explaining her pride.

questions.text: By the time the guests arrived, we        the table.
wrongReasons: Wrong auxiliary: had, not has, for a moment before another past point.
Missing "had" before the past participle.
Wrong tense/structure.
questions.explain: 'Just' shows this finished a short time before the guests arrived.

questions.text: He        that restaurant before, so he didn't know what to order.
wrongReasons: Wrong auxiliary: had, not has, for lack of experience before that past point.
Missing "had" before the past participle.
Wrong tense/structure.
questions.explain: An experience missing before a past point — past perfect.

questions.text: She        the news by the time I called her.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense/structure.
Wrong auxiliary: had, not has.
Missing "had" before the past participle.
questions.explain: 'By the time' signals the earlier of two past events.

questions.text: By the time the exam started, I        the last chapter.
wrongReasons: "By the time" points back to before another past moment — that needs hadn't, not didn't.
Wrong tense: haven't is present perfect — the exam is in the past, so use hadn't.
The past continuous describes an action in progress; here you need hadn't + past participle.
questions.explain: Negative past perfect: by the time the exam started, the reading still hadn't happened.

questions.text: They        the results by the time the meeting started.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: haven't is present perfect, not past perfect.
This needs hadn't to show the missing result came before another past point.
Wrong structure for a negative past perfect.
questions.explain: 'By the time' + negative past perfect: hadn't received.

questions.text: She was upset because she        enough time to prepare.
wrongReasons: Wrong auxiliary: the story is in the past, so use hadn't, not hasn't.
After hadn't, use the past participle (had), not the base form.
After didn't, the verb is never in the past form — and this needs hadn't + past participle.
questions.explain: 'Have' → 'had' as a past participle, so 'hadn't had' is correct.

questions.text: you ever visited Japan before that trip?
wrongReasons: Wrong auxiliary: did doesn't fit "ever visited...before that trip".
Wrong tense: have signals present perfect, not past perfect.
Wrong auxiliary for this structure.
questions.explain: Past perfect questions start with 'had', whatever the subject.

questions.text: she finished the report when you asked for it?
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: has signals present perfect, not past perfect.
Wrong auxiliary: did doesn't show which of two past moments came first.
Wrong auxiliary for this structure.
questions.explain: 'Had' + subject + past participle asks which past event came first.

questions.text: the train left when you reached the platform?
wrongReasons: "Were" goes with -ing or adjectives, not with a past participle like "left".
Wrong tense: have signals present perfect, not past perfect.
"Did" needs the base form ("leave"), and it doesn't show the train left before you arrived.
questions.explain: A question about which of two past events happened first: had + subject + past participle.

questions.text: By the time I got to the office, he        three letters.
wrongReasons: "By the time" needs had + past participle, not the past simple.
Wrong participle: the past participle of write is written, not wrote.
Wrong auxiliary: has instead of had.
questions.explain: 'Write' is irregular: write → wrote → written. The letters were finished before I arrived.

questions.text: He        the window before anyone noticed.
wrongReasons: Wrong participle: the past participle of break is broken, not broke.
Wrong auxiliary: has instead of had.
After had, use the past participle (broken), not the base form.
questions.explain: 'Break' is irregular: break → broke → broken.

questions.text: I        my homework before the teacher checked it.
wrongReasons: Wrong participle: the past participle of do is done, not did.
Wrong auxiliary: has instead of had.
After had, use the past participle (done), not the base form.
questions.explain: 'Do' is irregular: do → did → done.

questions.text: By the time we woke up, Dad        halfway to the coast.
wrongReasons: Wrong auxiliary: has instead of had.
Wrong participle: the past participle of drive is driven, not drove.
"By the time" needs had + past participle, not the past simple.
questions.explain: 'Drive' is irregular: drive → drove → driven. The driving was done before we woke up.

errorCorrection.title: Find the mistake
errorCorrection.subtitle: Each sentence has exactly one mistake. Tap the word you think is wrong. Twenty original sentences.

items.message: "Go" is irregular: the past participle is gone, not went.
"Steal" is irregular: the past participle is stolen, not stole.
"Begin" is irregular: the past participle is begun, not began.
"Forget" is irregular: the past participle is forgotten, not forgot.
"Choose" is irregular: the past participle is chosen, not chose.
Wrong auxiliary: an action before another past action needs had, not has.
Wrong auxiliary: the bell rang in the past, so the earlier action needs had, not have.
"By the time" + a past event needs the past perfect: had, not has.
"Before 2020" is a point in the past, so use had, not has.
Wrong auxiliary: had, not has, for an earlier past action.
"Since the summer" looks back from a past moment, so it needs the past perfect: hadn't seen, not didn't seen.
Wrong tense: for an action (not) done before another past point, use hadn't, not didn't.
"By ten o'clock" needs the past perfect negative: hadn't + past participle — hadn't woken, not didn't woke.
Wrong tense: "by the end of the exam" is a past point, so use hadn't, not didn't.
After hadn't, use the past participle — seen, not saw.
After hadn't, use the past participle — gone, not went.
After hadn't, use the past participle — eaten, not ate.
This is a regular verb — add -ed to make the past participle: cooked, not cook.
This is a regular verb — add -ed to make the past participle: ordered, not order.

levelCheck.title: How well do you know it?
levelCheck.subtitle: 20 mixed questions — typing, word order, irregular participles, multiple choice, and spot-the-mistake. One pass, then a breakdown of where you're strong and where to go back and practise.

items.sentText: By the time we got home, the rain {{blank}}.
items.explain: The rain stopped before we got home — 'by the time' needs had + past participle.

items.sentText: By the time the bus came, she {{blank}} her breakfast.
items.explain: Negative past perfect: hadn't + past participle. Breakfast was still unfinished when the bus came.

items.sentText: I was nervous that evening because I {{blank}} my girlfriend's parents before.
items.explain: 'Never' goes between had and the past participle: had never met. 'Meet' is irregular: met.

items.sentText: {{blank}} your sister ever been abroad before her school trip to Paris?
items.explain: 'Had' starts the question; 'been' is the past participle of be.

items.text: She {{blank}} the old letters away before I could read them.
wrongReasons: "Throw" is irregular: throw → threw → thrown. "Throwed" is a common learner mistake.
Wrong auxiliary: had, not has, for an earlier past action.
This is the -ing form, not the past participle.
items.explain: 'Throw' is irregular: throw → threw → thrown. Throwing the letters away came before I could read them.

items.text: He {{blank}} the book twice by the time the film came out.
wrongReasons: "Read" is irregular: read → read → read. "Readed" doesn't exist.
Wrong auxiliary: had, not has, for an earlier past action.
This is the -ing form, not the past participle.
items.explain: 'Read' looks the same in all three forms (read → read → read), but the participle is pronounced /red/. He read it before the film came out.

items.text: She {{blank}} the door before I could stop her.
wrongReasons: There's no such form as "shutted" — "shut" doesn't change: shut → shut → shut.
Wrong auxiliary: had, not has.
This is the -ing form, not the past participle.
items.explain: 'Shut' doesn't change: shut → shut → shut. Shutting came before I could stop her.

items.text: By the time we got to the river, my brother {{blank}} three fish.
wrongReasons: There's no such form as "catched" — "catch" is irregular: catch → caught.
Wrong auxiliary: had, not has, for an earlier past action.
This is the -ing form, not the past participle.
items.explain: 'Catch' is irregular: catch → caught → caught. He caught the fish before we arrived.

items.text: {{blank}} the baby fallen asleep when you got home?
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: have signals present perfect, not past perfect.
"Did" needs the base form ("fall"), not the past participle "fallen".
"Was" doesn't go with the past participle "fallen" here — the past perfect uses had.
items.explain: A past perfect question starts with 'had' + subject + past participle.

items.text: I didn't recognise him at first because he {{blank}} a beard since I last saw him.
wrongReasons: Wrong auxiliary: the story is in the past, so use had, not has.
"Since I last saw him" needs a perfect tense — the past simple doesn't work with "since".
The past continuous doesn't work with "since" here — you need had + past participle.
items.explain: Past perfect explains the reason: the beard grew before the moment I didn't recognise him.

items.text: He {{blank}} that song before, so he didn't recognise it.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: haven't is present perfect, not past perfect.
This needs hadn't, not didn't, to show it happened before another past point.
Wrong structure for a negative past perfect.
items.explain: Negative past perfect: hadn't + past participle.

items.text: By 8 a.m. the shop {{blank}} its doors.
wrongReasons: Wrong auxiliary: had, not has, for an action before a past point.
Missing "had" before the past participle.
Wrong tense/structure.
items.explain: 'Already' sits between had and the past participle.

items.message: "Speak" is irregular: the past participle is spoken, not spoke.
Wrong auxiliary: had, not have, for an action before another past point.
"By the time" + a past event needs the past perfect: hadn't packed, not didn't packed.
This is a regular verb — add -ed to make the past participle: arrived, not arrive.
